In [[mathematics]], in the theory of [[Module (mathematics)|module]]s, the '''radical''' of a module is a component in the theory of structure and classification.  It is a generalization of the [[Jacobson radical]] for [[ring (mathematics)|rings]].  In many ways, it is the [[duality (mathematics)|dual]] notion to that of the [[socle (mathematics)|socle]] soc(''M'') of ''M''.

==Definition==
Let <math>R</math> be a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] and <math>M</math> a left <math>R</math>-[[module (mathematics)|module]].  A [[submodule]] <math>N</math> of <math>M</math> is called '''[[maximal submodule|maximal]]''' or '''cosimple''' if the [[quotient module|quotient]] <math>M/N</math> is a [[simple module]].  The '''radical''' of the module <math>M</math> is the [[intersection (set theory)|intersection]] of all maximal submodules of <math>M</math>,
:<math>\mathrm{rad}(M) = \bigcap\, \{N \mid N \mbox{ is a maximal submodule of } M\}</math>
Equivalently,
:<math>\mathrm{rad}(M) = \sum\, \{S \mid S \mbox{ is a superfluous submodule of } M\}</math>
These definitions have direct dual analogues for <math>\mathrm{soc}(M)</math>.

==Properties==
* In addition to the fact that <math>\mathrm{rad}(M)</math> is the sum of superfluous submodules, in a [[Noetherian module]], <math>\mathrm{rad}(M)</math> itself is a [[superfluous submodule]]. 
In fact, if <math>M</math> is [[finitely generated module|finitely generated]] over a ring, then <math>\mathrm{rad}(M)</math> itself is a superfluous submodule. This is because any proper submodule of <math>M</math> is contained in a maximal submodule of <math>M</math> when <math>M</math> is finitely generated.
* A ring for which <math>\mathrm{rad}(M)=\{0\}</math> for every right <math>R</math>-module <math>M</math> is called a right [[V-ring (ring theory)|V-ring]]. 
* For any module <math>M</math>, <math>\mathrm{rad}(M/\mathrm{rad}(M))</math> is zero.
* <math>M</math> is a [[finitely generated module|finitely generated]] module [[if and only if]] the [[cosocle]] <math>M/\mathrm{rad}(M)</math> is finitely generated and <math>\mathrm{rad}(M)</math> is a superfluous submodule of <math>M</math>.
